title: Restore The Array
summary: Given a string s representing a sequence of digits and an integer k, determine the number of possible integer arrays that can be formed where each integer is in the range [1, k] and there are no leading zeros.
statement: Given a string s representing a sequence of digits and an integer k, determine the number of possible integer arrays that can be formed where each integer is in the range [1, k] and there are no leading zeros. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Split the digit string into integers from 1 through k with no leading zeroes.
Return the number of splits modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Let ways[i] count valid splits of the suffix beginning at i.
A suffix beginning with zero contributes none.
Extend a numeric piece until it exceeds k, adding ways after each valid endpoint.
Every restoration has a unique first piece, so this partitions the solution set without overlap.
editorial: Every restoration has a unique first piece, so this partitions the solution set without overlap.

tests.explanation: The whole string as integer 1000 is the only valid restoration.
Every possible piece after the initial one begins with zero, so no restoration exists.
